_comment: The parts of the compatibility contract that cannot be derived from test artifacts. Everything else on the status page is generated from CI output and the ratchet ledgers, so it cannot drift; these entries are hand-maintained and should be reviewed whenever a gate is added or a divergence closed.

divergences.title: pg_backend_pid() is not an OS process id
divergences.detail: pgrust is thread-per-backend, so there are no per-backend processes. It allocates a synthetic pid space (pg_stat_activity reports 1000, 1001, 1029, ...; /proc/<pid> exists for none of them). Anything that signals that pid from outside the server fails, including parts of upstream's own TAP suite. pg_cancel_backend and pg_terminate_backend work normally.

divergences.title: archive_library accepts a library it cannot load
divergences.detail: Setting archive_library to an unloadable name is accepted without complaint, so archiving silently never happens. This is the mechanism behind the contrib ledger's basic_archive entry. Until it is closed, archive-based backup cannot be claimed safe to configure by hand.

divergences.title: pg_ctl restart fails unless the stack limit is raised in the environment
divergences.detail: pgrust needs a large stack (it runs with max_stack_depth=60000 and ulimit -s 65520). The Docker entrypoint raises the limit itself, so the normal container start works. But pgrust writes its real binary path into postmaster.opts, so `pg_ctl restart` re-execs it directly, inherits whatever stack limit the shell had, and dies with 'invalid value for parameter max_stack_depth ... must not exceed 7680kB'. Any operator restarting via pg_ctl rather than the entrypoint hits this. Set the limit at the container or service level (docker --ulimit stack=67092480, or LimitSTACK= in a systemd unit).

absent: No stable extension ABI; existing PostgreSQL extensions do not load.
PL/Python, PL/Perl and PL/Tcl are not ported. PL/pgSQL is.
No in-place major-version upgrade. A wrong-version data directory is refused.
The JIT targets Graviton4; other platforms run but without comparable performance.
